A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FastDINOv2 and contain complete main text, Tables 1–12, Figures 1–5, and Appendix A.1–A.7. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original training, accuracy, corruption robustness, instance recognition, and segmentation experiments in Section 4, plus ablations and SimCLR experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix A, including FastDINOv2 evaluations and the SimCLR/FastSimCLR comparison in Table 10.

M1.justification: Both versions specify the same two-stage resolution curriculum, optimizer restart, positional-embedding interpolation, and second-stage Gaussian noise patching. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both use ImageNet-100, ImageNet-1K and their corruption variants, Oxford and Paris instance recognition, and ADE20K segmentation. Appendix experiments retain the same data and task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain identical DINOv2 baselines and comparison variants. Appendix Table 10 retains the same SimCLR versus FastSimCLR comparison.

E3.justification: Reported data selections, crop resolutions, model configurations, training budgets, batch sizes, metrics, and evaluation procedures are unchanged throughout Section 4 and Appendix A.

E4.justification: The resolution, batch-size, positional-embedding, and transition-schedule ablations are retained unchanged. Fourier sensitivity, Grad-CAM, and convergence-time analyses also contain the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–12 and the graphical findings match. For example, Table 1 retains DINOv2/FastDINOv2 clean accuracies of 77.8%/76.2% and ImageNet-C errors of 56.5%/56.7%.

T1.justification: The crop definition in Equation 1 and bicubic interpolation mathematics in Appendix A.3, Equations 2–4, are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about faster pretraining, computational savings, robustness, and competitive clean accuracy. Contribution scope and claimed novelty are unchanged.

C2.justification: The frequency-bias explanations, corruption tradeoffs, and interpretations of downstream performance remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitation concerning the fixed transition schedule and the same future directions.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, hardware, training-time information, and preprocessing details are unchanged. The supplied code-access link is also identical.

R1.justification: The same 39 cited works and related-work discussion are retained. Reference 2 changes title wording but retains arXiv identifier 2312.02366; bibliography metadata edits do not change the cited work or research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 shortens bibliography entries by removing many page ranges, publisher details, and some identifiers or URLs, and revises reference title wording and capitalization. The arXiv version/date stamp changes, while the main narrative and appendix structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Shortened references change line wrapping, spacing, and pagination within pages 10–13, with minor spacing changes around Section 5. All figures and tables retain their content, appearance, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 leaves the scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and appendices unchanged. Shorter bibliography entries trade some bibliographic detail for compactness, but these editorial and layout changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
